1.

Proceedings have arisen from filing of DAR in FIR No. 437/15 of PS Anand Vihar, registered u/s 279/338 IPC, in respect of an accident dated 21.06.2015 wherein petitioner Deepika Bhatia suffered grievous injuries including severe head injury.
As per the facts, on 21.06.2015, at about 06 :15 PM injured/petitioner Deepika was crossing the road near cross river mall, near Karkardooma courts.

Respondent no. 1 Pulkit Aggarwal was allegedly driving the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-14CM-4444 Maruti Suzuki Ertiga, in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner which resulted in MACT No.1373/2016 Page 1 causing of grievous injuries including head injury.

Petitioner was taken to Dr. Hedgewar hospital, where her MLC no. 1950/15 was prepared and later she was shifted to MAX superspecialty hospital Patparganj.
2.
In response to the DAR, owner and driver filed the reply / written statement wherein it is denied that accident took place due to rash and reckless driving of respondent no. 1.
It is pleaded that vehicle in question was fully insured with National Insurance co. ltd.
Vide policy no.
It is stated that driver was having valid DL.

Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
1 3.
Reply/

written statement has also been filed by respondent no.3/ insurance company, wherein insurance company took all the plea in terms of Section 134 (c), 147/149, 157,66 nad 88 of Motor Vehicle Act and further pleaded that insurance company reserved right to take appropriate defence as per Section 170 M V Act.
It is not disputed however, that the vehicle in question was duly insured with respondent no. 3.
It is pleaded that petitioner is required to prove the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.

4. On the basis as come on the record, on 19.04.2016 following issues were framed by Ld.
Predecessor of this court:
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.DL-14CM-4444 on 21.06.2015 at 6.00 pm in front of Cross River Mall, Main Road, Anand Vihar, Delhi in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against petitioner who sustained injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
OPP (3)Relief.
MACT No.1373/2016 Page 2

5 . During the course of proceedings, interim compensation amount was awarded by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 17.07.2017 for Rs. 25,000/-.
6.

Since it came on the record by medical documents as well as disability certificate which was to the extent of 100 % and tribunal noted that due to the accidental injuries, petitioner remained in vegetative state, therefore upon an application under Order 32 Rule 5 CPC, Ld. Predecessor of this tribunal vide order dated 26.04.2017 appointed father of the petitioner Sh. Gulshan Bhatia as legal guardian/next friend of petitioner on the ground that she is 100% disable.

7. In order to prove her case, the petitioner examined five witnesses under:
(i) PW1 is Kuldeep S/o Babulal who is eye witness to the accident and deposed regarding the manner in which accident took place.
and further stated that immediately after the accident they were taken to Dr.Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan where MLC of him as well as of his son no.422/2017 and 421/2017 were prepared.
Witness proved his medical treatment record as Ex.PW1/1, medical bills as Ex.PW1/2, Aadhar card as Ex.PW1/3 and attested copy of DAR as Ex.PW1/4.
PW1 stated that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of tempo no.DL 1LV 1735.

(ii) PW-2 is Gulshan Bhatia father of the petitioner, who testify regarding the accident, nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner as well as regarding the medical expenses, and other expenses incurred on account of the injuries of the petitioenor and the fact that petitioner due to head injuries, is 100% disabled and in a vegetative condition.

Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
2 MACT No.1373/2016 Page 3
(iii) PW3 is Dr. P P Singh, and PW-4 DR Dinesh Kumar Stai from GTB hospital both of them have deposed regarding disability certificate of the petitioner Deepika Bhatia.
(iv) PW-5 is Sh.Tushar Diwan from Tata Consultancy Services, who proved the salaries slips of Deepika Bhatia from January 2015 to July 2015.
8. On the other hand, no evidence has been led either on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 or on behalf of respondent no. 3/ insurance.
9. I have heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire evidence and material placed on record.
I have also gone though written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner as well as Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3/ insurance.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE No.1 10.
It is well settled that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
At the same time it be noted that the Tribunal is also to examine the evidence, more particularly when defence of contributory negligence has been raised by the respondents.
11. In this case, on behalf of insurance company plea of contributory negligence has been pleaded as well as argued.

Ld. MACT No.1373/2016 Page 4 Counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3 submitted that petitioner/injured was crossing main road without caring the traffic and there was no zebra crossing, where from she was crossing the road.
Injured suddenly came in front of offending vehicle which resulted into an accident.

It is submitted that evidence of eye witness PW1 is unworthy of any reliance because he admits in his evidence that he left the spot without waiting for the police and went to the police station after 3/4 days.

It is submitted that even site plan annexed with the DAR also indicate that accident took place in the middle of the road clearly showing that injured was crossing the road in violation of traffic rules and accident took place in middle of the road.

As such injured/petitioner is liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 50%.
12.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner on the other hand submitted that evidence of PW1 as well as other evidence on the record clearly establish rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
13.
Before we discuss the evidence on the record, it is appropriate to understand the scope of defence 'contributory negligence' taken by the respondents in motor accident claim cases.

Contributory negligence consists of the absence of that ordinary care which a sentient being ought Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
3 reasonably to have taken for his own safety, and which had it been exercised would have enable him to avoid the injury of which he complains, or the doing of some act which he ought not to have done and but for which the calamity would not have occurred.

Wakelin v. London and South Western Ry.
Co. (1886) 12 AC 41.

entities.text:
Wakelin v. London and South Western Ry.
Co. (1886) 12 AC 41
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The basic principles of Contributory negligence in the field of accident under the MACT No.1373/2016 Page 5 Motor Vehicle Act is that when the defendants prove that the plaintiff has failed to take precautions against the possible danger and that those precautions, if taken, would have been effective to protect against the danger which occurred.
Salmond in his book has given a classic example regarding the motorists.
That is quoted below:

"A motorist who drives straight across a light-controlled crossing against the red light and knocks down a pedestrian who has begun to cross in reliance on the lights but without looking over his right shoulder cannot be heard to say that the pedestrian is thereby guilty of Contributory negligence as against him, though such conduct on the part of the pedestrian might attract that description if he had been knocked down by a motorist lawfully turning left with the green light in his favour."

14. So, the law is that if it is proved on record that there is negligence on the part of the claimant the amount of compensation that he is entitled will certainly be reduced to the extent or for which he is negligent.

However tribunal must have to ensure that there is evidence proving injured contributing to incidence of accident, in other words evidence must establish that accident would not have occurred, but for negligence of injured also.
It be noted that contributory negligence cannot be inferred, rather must be established even if by preponderance of probability.

In Black's Law Dictionary, Fifth Edition, the meaning of Contributory negligence has been given as follows :
"Contributory negligence.

The act or omission amounting to want of ordinary care on part of complaining party, which, concurring with defendant's negligence , is proximate cause of injury..."
MACT No.1373/2016 Page 6 15.

In the facts of the present case petitioner examined PW1 Kuldeep who deposed that on 21.07.2015 while he was going in a car to show the same to his customer near McDonald's, Cross River Mall, offending vehicle Maruti Suzuki Ertiga no.DL 14CM 4444 came in a rash and negligent manner from Vivek Vihar side.
Said offending vehicle crossed over the car of PW1 and then hit the lady namely Deepika Bhatia.
Thereafter car stopped on the road side, driver came out of the car.
PW1 identified respondent no.1, present in the Tribunal.

16. Having considered the submissions and taking note of the evidence, it be noted that evidence of PW1 is consistent not only with regard to the high speed with which the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1.
Witness stated that the offending vehicle was cross over by his vehicle and thereafter hit the injured.
It has come on the record that injured was trying to cross over the road.

It be noted that it is not in every case where injured was crossing over the road, injured would as a thumb Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
4 rule consider to be liable for contributory negligence.
Defence of contributory negligence as noted above was required to be proved.
In this case evidence of PW1 is consistent, nothing came in the cross-examination of PW1 even to suggest that the injured was contributory negligent while crossing over the road.
17. It be noted that no evidence has been led either from respondent no.1 and 2 (owner, driver) or from insurance company/ respondent no.3.
Driver of the offending vehicle has not been called upon in the witness box for reasons best known to the respondents to prove the defence of contributory negligence if any.
In such situation when nothing has come in the evidence of PW1 to prove contributory negligence, nor any MACT No.1373/2016 Page 7 witness has been examined by respondents.
Mere arguing on the plea of contributory negligence on the basis of site plan annexed with the DAR, in the opinion of this Tribunal is not sufficient to prove such defence.

18. Even otherwise when it has come on the record in the evidence of PW1 that the offending vehicle was being driven in a very high speed, hitting a person in between the road clearly shows that the vehicle was in such a high speed that driver could not control the speed and hit the injured in between the road.
Thus, the site plan also indicate rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent no.1.
There is also mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle on the record in which it is mentioned that there was fresh dent on the bonnet which,
apparently
occurred due to the impact of striking the vehicle to the injured, when it was in a very high speed

. 
19. In Indian scenario, where there is no sufficient facilities on road for crossing over or not sufficient zebra crossing, Tribunal cannot assume or infer contributory negligence only for the reason that injured was crossing over the road and was hit by the offending vehicle.

In this case it has already come that the offending vehicle was being driven in a very high speed, driver of the vehicle like car is expected to take necessary precautions while driving on Indian roads, to foresee a possibility of someone trying to cross over the road.
Therefore in such circumstances in the absence of any evidence, defence of contributory negligence, has not been proved.
Rather this Tribunal concludes that accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 which resulted into causing grievous injuries to petitioner.
As such issue no.1 stands MACT No.1373/2016 Page 8 in favour of claimant and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 20.
Issue no.2 involves question of computation of amount of compensation payable to petitioner as well as the question of liability regarding the payment of compensation.

At the outset it be noted that Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
5 compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 21.
The present case pertains to the injury to Deepika Bhatia.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) MACT No.1373/2016 Page 9 loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.
22. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his MACT No.1373/2016 Page 10 inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
6
as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:

Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities MACT No.1373/2016 Page 11 (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
23.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:
24.
It is matter of record that petitioner/injured in the accident suffered grievous injuries including severe head injury.

Due to which petitioner remained in semi coma condition and has been in a Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
7
persistent vegetative state.
During the course of proceedings her medical conditions were examined by medical board and medical board issued

disability certificate no.215/75/ 203/17 dated 20.03.2017, which is on record and Ex.PW1/Q, as per which permanent disability has been assessed to be 100%, it is mentioned that injured cannot be evacuated (in a semi coma state).

PW2 has deposed that immediately after the accident she was taken to Dr.Hedgewar hospital where her MLC was prepared and later she got treatment in Max Super Specialty hospital Patparganj from 21.06.2015 to 22.07.2015.
On 24.06.2015 petitioner was tracheostomised.
Copy of discharge summary is Ex.PW2/M.
Medical certificate of treating doctor Dr.H.S. Bhatoe is Ex.PW2/N.
PW2 has stated that he has spent about Rs.12,62,332/- for medical expenses, medicines etc.

Medical bills are collectively exhibited as Ex.PW2/R and expenses incurred on physiotherapy since September 2015 is of Rs.2,74,700/- which is proved by invoices/bills Ex.PW2/T.
25.
Nothing came in the cross-examination of PW2 on this aspect except a suggestion denying the medical expenditure MACT No.1373/2016 Page 12 and expense on physiotherapy.

Taking into consideration the fact that the injured is permanently disabled to the extent of 100% and medical bills collectively Ex.PW2/R which include invoices for medicines, pharmacy as well as expenses incurred for treatment in Max Super Specialty Hospital
. In that hospital she was subjected to diagnostic test including MRI, X-ray etc. and was also tracheostomised.
Bills Ex.PW2/R have not been substantively disputed by respondent no.3.

Similarly taking into consideration medical condition of the injured as she has been in a semi coma condition and unresponsive state, therefore the bill regarding physiotherapy Ex.PW2/T conducted on her are also very much proved on the record.

Thus taking into consideration entire bills on record, this Tribunal finds that petitioner has duly established by preponderance of probabilities the total medical expenditure of sum of Rs.15,37,032/-.

Loss of future earning due to disability :
26.

As it has been noted above that on account of the accidental injuries, petitioner has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 100% on account of her being in a vegetative state and being continuously under semi coma condition.
Her medical condition, disability certificate has been proved by evidence of PW3 Dr.P.P. Singh and PW4 Dr.Dinesh Kumar Satti.

PW4 testified that as per disability certificate patient could not be evaluated for hearing impairment as she was in a coma and was not in a position to respond to test signal because of her disability.
PW4 also testified that permanent disability was assessed to 100% as patient was severe spastic quaderplagia with E1VTM1.
PW4 further says that injured was not in a position to her eyes, speak or move her limbs.
She was taking breath MACT No.1373/2016 Page 13 through a tube placed in her neck and is being fed through tube placed through nose.
27. From the evidence of PW3 and PW4 as well as MLC and evidence of PW2, it has come on the record that after receiving the accidental injuries, injured/petitioner is in coma since then till date.
Moreover doctors have found that there is least chances of her improvement, therefore medical board assessed the permanent disability of injured to be 100%.

In view of the evidence as come on the record it is evident that injured is not only in medical terms, permanently disabled but is 100%
functional disabled.

On account of such 100% disability, petitioner is unable to move from bed Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
8 without assistance.
As such while this Tribunal would compute the loss of earning/ income, such computation would be assessed almost on same manner as in case anyone dies after the roadside accident.

28. In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr.
(2011) 1 SCC 343

Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr.
(2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down that while assessing the permanent disability of an injured of road side accident, Tribunal must assess the disablement affecting the functioning of the injured, in the light of the work/ service/activities in which injured is involved for his livelihood.
In present case, as noted above this Tribunal has already found that medical as well as functional disability of petitioner as 100%.
29. Therefore amount of loss of earning of an injured having 100% permanent disability would be in the same manner as in case of death by road side accident.

In death cases, the MACT No.1373/2016 Page 14 guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

sentences.text:
30. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
Age 31.
In view of evidence of Ex.PW2/C i.e. CBSE certificate of injured, as per which the date of birth of injured is 23.09.1976.
Injured completed her B.A. Hons in English from DU in 1997, copy of Degree is Ex.PW2/D.
As such at the time of accident on 21.06.2015 age of injured was around 39 years of age.
Income of injured 32.

It has come on record by way of evidence of PW2 Gulshan Bhatia that at the time of accident injured Deepika Bhatia was working with Tata Consultancy Services as Business Process Lead and her last drawn gross salary for month of June 2015 was Rs.42,747/-.
Pay slips for month of April to June 2015 are collectively Ex.PW2/I.
PW2 further testified that his daughter was an income tax payee.

Copies of Form 16 for assessment year 2014 and 2015 are collectively exhibited as Ex.PW2/J.
Copy of ITR for assessment year 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15
are collectively Ex.PW2/L.

Beside the evidence of PW2, petitioner has also examined PW5 Tushar Diwan, Assistant MACT No.1373/2016 Page 15 Manager from Tata Consultancy Services who proved the salary slip of petitioner Deepika Bhatia from January 2015 to July 2015 which are Ex.PW5/1.

Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
9 33.

From the above noted evidence of PW2 and PW5 as well as the documents proved in their evidence including her office identity card Ex.PW2/H, salary slips Ex.PW2/I as well as ITRs collectively Ex.PW2/L and Ex.PW5/1, it is established on the record that at the time of accident injured/petitioner was drawing salary of Rs.42,747/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:
34.
As the injured is around 39 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation in terms of judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 which is 15.

Future Prospects:
35.

In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra),
in the present case injured is entitled for future prospects to the extent of 50% as injured is below 40 years of age at the time of accident.

36. As such when this Tribunal found from the evidence that the monthly income of the injured is Rs.42,747/- if it is added with 50% of the same for future prospects, then it comes to be Rs.42,747 +
Rs.21,373.50 which comes out to be Rs.64,120.5 per month.

Applying the multiplier of 15, the amount of compensation on account of loss of income is assessed to be Rs.1,15,41,690/-
(Rs.64,120.5 X 12 X 15 X 100 divided by 100).
Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
37. So far as special diet given to petitioner/injured is concerned, PW2 deposed that injured has to be fed a special diet MACT No.1373/2016 Page 16 through feeding tube.
He proved copy of diet plan as Ex.PW2/U.
PW2 also deposed that he employed a cook/maid at home to prepare food and assist the nurse in feeding the petitioner and made expenditure of Rs.2,70,000/- till date.
No basis has been given for claiming conveyance charges.
38. Perusal of diet plan Ex.PW2/U shows that it is not a prescription slip prescribed any doctor or hospital advising any type of special diet to be given to petitioner/injured.

This document are just papers mentioning diet and supplements allegedly to be given to injured, however this document is not on the letter head of any doctor or hospital prescribing the same nor it has been signed by any doctor.
In the absence of any concrete proof of giving special diet to petitioner, this Tribunal is of the view that the amount claimed by the petitioner is exaggerated.
However keeping in view the evidence as come on record, it is duly proved that petitioner/injured is in vegetative state since the day of accident.
Thus, this Tribunal presumes that some special diet must have been given to the petitioner.
So this Tribunal assesses the amount of compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

Attendant Charges:
39.

PW2 Gulshan Bhatia deposed in his evidence that for better treatment of his daughter/injured, a sum of Rs.17,14,920/- was incurred on nursing aids w.e.f. 30.06.2015 vide invoices/ vouchers Ex.PW2/S (colly.)

Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
10 40.
Perusal invoices/bills Ex.PW2/S (colly.) show that a total sum of Rs.2,82,000/- was spent on nursing aid of petitioner/injured.

Petitioner is not only entitled for above amount, but is also entitled for future attendant charges, in view MACT No.1373/2016 Page 17 of the judgment as relied upon by ld. counsel for petitioner of Hon'ble High Court in Pritam Singh vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
& Ors. 2016 SCC OnLine Del 2147, wherein it is held that in case where the injured has suffered 100% permanent disability, there can be no doubt that even in future also attendant would be required throughout life and Hon'ble High Court awarded future attendant charges on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled worker.

entities.text:
Pritam Singh vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
& Ors. 2016 SCC OnLine Del 2147
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case also injured is 100% permanently disabled and would be dependent on attendant for her future life also.

Therefore petitioner in the opinion of this Tribunal is also entitled for future charges for minimum wages of unskilled worker i.e.
Rs.10,440/- X 12 X 15 which is Rs.18,79,200/-.
If this amount Rs.18,79,200/- is added with bill Rs.2,82,000/-, total comes out to be Rs.21,61,200/-.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings:
41.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No: 709/02, date of decision:
02.02.2007 can be considered:
"On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.
The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be: (a) Nature of injury; (b) Body part affected; (c) Duration of the treatment."
42. In this case, as per medical documents of MACT No.1373/2016 Page 18 petitioner/injured placed on record, she suffered 100% permanent disability.
It is matter of record that petitioner is in vegetative state since the day of accident.

Therefore taking into consideration medical condition of the injured as she has been in a semi coma condition and unresponsive state, considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, this Tribunal finds that claimant is entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/- on account of pain and suffering.

Loss of Amenities:
43.
It is evident on record that the petitioner is living separately from her husband along with her minor children at the house of her father (PW2).
As per medical documents petitioner suffered 100% permanent disability and she is in vegetative state since the day of accident.
The treatment of claimant as per evidence on the record is running till now.
As such this Tribunal finds that it would be just and proper if compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded to petitioner under this head.

11 44.

4. On the basis as come on the record, on 19.04.2016 following issues were framed by Ld.
Predecessor of this court:
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle bearing no.DL-14CM-4444 on 21.06.2015 at 6.00 pm in front of Cross River Mall, Main Road, Anand Vihar, Delhi in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against petitioner who sustained injuries?
OPP (2)Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE No.1 10.
It is well settled that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
At the same time it be noted that the Tribunal is also to examine the evidence, more particularly when defence of contributory negligence has been raised by the respondents.
Contributory negligence consists of the absence of that ordinary care which a sentient being ought Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/
3 reasonably to have taken for his own safety, and which had it been exercised would have enable him to avoid the injury of which he complains, or the doing of some act which he ought not to have done and but for which the calamity would not have occurred.
Wakelin v. London and South Western Ry.
Co. (1886) 12 AC 41.
14. So, the law is that if it is proved on record that there is negligence on the part of the claimant the amount of compensation that he is entitled will certainly be reduced to the extent or for which he is negligent.
However tribunal must have to ensure that there is evidence proving injured contributing to incidence of accident, in other words evidence must establish that accident would not have occurred, but for negligence of injured also.
It be noted that contributory negligence cannot be inferred, rather must be established even if by preponderance of probability.
In this case evidence of PW1 is consistent, nothing came in the cross-examination of PW1 even to suggest that the injured was contributory negligent while crossing over the road.
Driver of the offending vehicle has not been called upon in the witness box for reasons best known to the respondents to prove the defence of contributory negligence if any.
In such situation when nothing has come in the evidence of PW1 to prove contributory negligence, nor any MACT No.1373/2016 Page 7 witness has been examined by respondents.
Mere arguing on the plea of contributory negligence on the basis of site plan annexed with the DAR, in the opinion of this Tribunal is not sufficient to prove such defence.
18. Even otherwise when it has come on the record in the evidence of PW1 that the offending vehicle was being driven in a very high speed, hitting a person in between the road clearly shows that the vehicle was in such a high speed that driver could not control the speed and hit the injured in between the road.
Thus, the site plan also indicate rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent no.1.
occurred due to the impact of striking the vehicle to the injured, when it was in a very high speed
. 
19. In Indian scenario, where there is no sufficient facilities on road for crossing over or not sufficient zebra crossing, Tribunal cannot assume or infer contributory negligence only for the reason that injured was crossing over the road and was hit by the offending vehicle.
In this case it has already come that the offending vehicle was being driven in a very high speed, driver of the vehicle like car is expected to take necessary precautions while driving on Indian roads, to foresee a possibility of someone trying to cross over the road.
Therefore in such circumstances in the absence of any evidence, defence of contributory negligence, has not been proved.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 21.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
As such while this Tribunal would compute the loss of earning/ income, such computation would be assessed almost on same manner as in case anyone dies after the roadside accident.
28. In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr.
(2011) 1 SCC 343
29. Therefore amount of loss of earning of an injured having 100% permanent disability would be in the same manner as in case of death by road side accident.
In death cases, the MACT No.1373/2016 Page 14 guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Application of Multiplier:
34.
As the injured is around 39 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation in terms of judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 which is 15.
In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra),
in the present case injured is entitled for future prospects to the extent of 50% as injured is below 40 years of age at the time of accident.
Petitioner is not only entitled for above amount, but is also entitled for future attendant charges, in view MACT No.1373/2016 Page 17 of the judgment as relied upon by ld. counsel for petitioner of Hon'ble High Court in Pritam Singh vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
& Ors. 2016 SCC OnLine Del 2147, wherein it is held that in case where the injured has suffered 100% permanent disability, there can be no doubt that even in future also attendant would be required throughout life and Hon'ble High Court awarded future attendant charges on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled worker.
Therefore taking into consideration medical condition of the injured as she has been in a semi coma condition and unresponsive state, considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, this Tribunal finds that claimant is entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/- on account of pain and suffering.
